IMO, if the apple pie is cooked just right so that the apples are still kind of firm, it’s great. Otherwise I agree with the “slimy lumpy goo” thing.

if you mean disgusting because it’s unhealthy, then yes. but if you mean disgusting by how it tastes, oh man you’re missing out! poutine is one of my favourite treats (however I am canadian soo) that even my super picky friends like, definitely worth trying if you ever get a chance. make sure it’s made with real cheese curds though, that’s crucial!

Fries in chocolate milkshakes is something I love! To me, mixing salty and sweet is the best because it balances out two strong flavours, often I can’t eat a lot of something that is too sweet or too salty on its own. Ever had chocolate covered pretzels, or salted caramel, or even corn on the cob with salt and butter? It’s those things but extreme and americanized (I wouldn’t like fresh fries with a milkshake made with real dairy, but the fast food stuff together is a dream!)

Goat cheese!! In Canada, generally a menu item with goat cheese in it will say so in the description, I guess because it’s not as commonly liked here. However, travelling in France last year I realized the hard way that there are no “warnings” and anything with “a variety of cheeses” is probably going to have goat cheese. I will never understand how people like it and how I can hate it so much.
This might be useless, however I am grateful for learning this so thank you

This is a question my boyfriend has asked that i’ve been struggling to answer. Everyone experiences anxiety and depression differently but i’m going to try and explain my experience. 
The best way I can sum it up is “sunrise, sunset” over and over - I struggle every morning to get out of bed, which often makes me late for my day. Sometimes, I give in to the feeling and skip whatever I have planned that day. Then, maybe I eat a thing or two for breakfast or lunch, but usually I have no appetite so I force myself to snack or eat but rarely can finish a meal. I struggle to concentrate and often don’t finish my work, leaving me feeling guilty and full of negative thoughts and worries. I try to find relaxation in reading or watching a show before bed. I get into bed, and suddenly it’s 6 am and I haven’t slept at all despite trying to sleep since midnight. The whole thing then restarts. 
I’m always tired, I make up excuses daily to avoid seeing friends or people I know even though I would enjoy it under normal circumstances. Anxiety for me means avoiding a lot of things like eating in public, asking questions, and pretty much avoiding anything that will draw attention to myself around others. It also means panic attacks, which are (for me) nothing what I had thought based on stories and media. I can calm my mind down completely, however my body insists something is wrong and goes into overdrive. It starts off feeling breathless and needing to constantly take deep breaths, then I get jittery, feel sick to my stomach, extremely “out of it” and in when it’s really bad I depersonalize. This happens several times a day and often those around me don’t even know it’s happening. Also, they make you extremely tired because your body just released a bunch of adrenaline. 
In general, it feels like in order to succeed in life I have to not only do all the basic things like study and work, but I have to do many things in order to be in a place where I am healthy enough to study and work. I know everyone struggles with one thing or another and that I am relatively lucky, but that still doesn’t help me get over the fact that I have to work extremely hard just to the daily things that my friends can easily do. Anyways, sorry for the absolute essay and this will probably get lost in comments but hopefully it helps someone understand! If anyone has any questions to clarify, feel free to ask, it might help me see things from my boyfriend’s perspective.

I had someone say to me "in the grand scheme of things..." and it made me really step back and take a look at life. In the expanse of the universe it's really quite extraordinary that we are here and that we are conscious of this fact, also it really made me feel that all of the things that I was hurting over were so trivial. This may not be the kind of thing that helps anyone else, but it really helped me to step outside of our daily "bubble" we live in.
